submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on a restricted set of unit-opening stems and word-initial fragments (fire, Wind, Sand, Fen, Thunder, Ded, opens, integ, due, up, come, Red, Boston, Chris, G, and the hyphen inside such units) exactly when the prefix up to and including the token forms the still-incomplete left half of a stereotyped multi-token unit: a tokenizer-split word (Sand|well, Fen|way, Thunder|bolt, Ded|ication, opens|ource) or a frozen collocation (due|to, up|to, come|from, fire|extinguisher, Red|Sox, Boston|Red, first-name|surname, G|damn, up|front, Wind|turbines in power-grid context). The identical token stays weak or silent when its phrase is already complete (camp fire burned, was due yesterday, friend Chris arrived, topic-less sentence-initial Wind), and the pole never fires on compound openers outside this trigger set (chicken broth, Manchester United, coast road, Schedule B, water/dam/boats passages) or on the completion pieces themselves (well, way, bolt, ication, Sox).
